content_of_post_to_comment: People bemoan the fact that kids today get far less unstructured, unsupervised time than in the past, and I share this feeling. But I was talking with a parent about this, and her pushback was that in many (most?) cases, the alternative to supervised, structured activities will in practice be screen time. At least structured extracurriculars and family outings get kids out of the house, off screens, and socializing. Seems like a tough dilemma for parents.
comment: The tradeoff may be less about unstructured time versus activities and more about whether kids have ownership. A self-chosen hobby can build agency in ways a packed schedule often cannot.
